messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — multiple support tickets and internal alerts about p95/p99 latency regression for hosted /v1/generate in us-east-1 starting ~2024-06-18T08:12:00Z. Customers: AcmeCorp, ShopLoop. Symptoms: p95 from ~180ms -> ~1.2s, p99 from ~320ms -> ~3.8s, 5xx rate up from 0.6% -> 1.8%. No major error spike (most are timeouts/late responses). Anyone oncall?

Kevin Patel: oncall here. seeing the same in grafana — tail latency climbs coincide with a spike in long-running KV-cache misses on the runtime nodes. CPU on some pods up to 95% and GPU utilisation stable. Probably serving-side queuing.

Jason Rivera: I pulled a couple traces from x-ray: requests with long tail show repeated KV cache misses then fallback to full KV recompute which is expensive. stack: runtime v2.3.1, model redwood-medium-1, seq len typical 512.

Support Bot: Alert: incident 2024-06-18-LE-47 created. Pager duty: oncall. Link: https://alerts.redwood.internal/LE-47

Lisa Gomez: quick repro (customer sample):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium-1","input":"long prompt...","max_tokens":512}' 

# Response observed: 200 OK but streaming took ~3.5s for last tokens
```

Maria Chen: good repro. Impacting both streaming and non-streaming. Support reports higher complaints from bursty clients that hit a lot of cold KV prefixes.

Kevin Patel: quick checklist for mitigation (I executed 1 and 2 already):
1) Increase route-level concurrency cap to reduce queuing (temporary): `PATCH /admin/routes/generate {"concurrency_cap": 300}` — applied to us-east-1 at 08:18 UTC.
2) Flip circuit-breaker to "fast-fail->fallback" for /v1/generate for bronze tier to protect infra: `POST /admin/cb/toggle {"route":"/v1/generate","mode":"fallback","fallback_model":"redwood-small-1"}` — applied 08:20 UTC.
3) Enable prefix-KV prewarm for top 500 prefixes seen in last 24h (deferred).
4) If latency persists, throttle bursty API keys with rate-limiter rule.

Jason Rivera: after the cb->fallback flip I can see p95 down to ~420ms within 2 minutes. p99 still ~1.1s but trending down. Fallback model returns less costly tokens but maintains app-level correctness for most callers. :thumbsup:

SRE Alert Bot: Metric snapshot at 08:25 UTC: p95=430ms, p99=1.12s, 5xx=0.9% (was 1.8%).

Lisa Gomez: patch for guardrail policy I'm proposing — add to runtime config so next time we auto-fallback when route p95 > 600ms for 3 consecutive 1m buckets:
```
{
  "route":"/v1/generate",
  "slo":{
    "p95_ms":600,
    "evaluation_window":"60s",
    "breach_count_threshold":3
  },
  "on_breach":{
    "action":"fallback_model",
    "model":"redwood-small-1",
    "notify":"#eng-sre"
  }
}
```

Maria Chen: +1 on that guardrail. Also add an emergency rate-limit action to apply per-api-key throttles (burst_n / sustained_rps) for top offenders. Suggest default throttles: burst 50 req/min, sustained 5 rps when triggered.

Kevin Patel: implemented an interim throttling rule for the 12 API keys with highest request rates (applied 08:28 UTC). Monitoring now.

Jason Rivera: logs show reduced queue depth after throttle + cb fallback. KV prewarm job started for top 500 prefixes at 08:35 UTC (nice).

Support Bot: Notifying affected customers: AcmeCorp, ShopLoop, SmallBizX. Support ticket updates queued.

Maria Chen: long-term followups for postmortem:
- root cause: runtime KV cache pressure + sudden bursty traffic pattern; consider changing cache eviction policy and prewarm strategy.
- infra: add autoscale policy tuning to add runtime pods earlier on queue depth metric instead of CPU.
- product: add per-route cost/latency budgets and self-serve circuit-breaker toggles for customers.

Lisa Gomez: adding playbook steps into /runbooks/latency-regressions.md (short version):
- Detect: p95 > threshold -> create incident auto.
- Mitigate (fast): enable cb fallback to lower-latency model; apply per-key throttles; increase concurrency cap on route.
- Stabilize: prewarm prefixes; adjust autoscale on queue depth; schedule postmortem.
- Prevent: SLO guardrails (json above), metric alarms, and test harness for KV cold-starts.

Kevin Patel: current status 08:50 UTC: p95=210ms, p99=430ms, 5xx=0.45%. Will keep monitoring for 60m. Removing emergency throttles once stable.

Jason Rivera: opening postmortem ticket now with root-cause hypothesis and timeline. TAGS: latency, p95, p99, cb-fallback, kv-cache.

Maria Chen: thanks team. Action items: Lisa — merge guardrail PR by EOD; Kevin — monitor and roll back throttles when safe; Jason — postmortem draft by tomorrow; Support — customer comms. Marking this thread resolved once p99 < 600ms for 1h. :white_check_mark:
